column1: # npm-pre-scan evaluation corpus — REAL MALICIOUS PAYLOADS (stratified sample, static only)
# Purpose : stratified random sample for Layer 1 static-analysis breadth (no Docker, so it is cheap to run at this size).
#           Sample zips live at samples/npm/<id> in that repo and are ENCRYPTED
#           with the password `infected`. `id` below is the repo-relative path
#           under samples/npm/ — the package name and version are the two path
#           components before the filename (scoped names are stored `@scope@name`
#           in the directory but `@scope_name` in the filename, hence storing the
#           full path rather than reconstructing it).
#           Enumerated from the samples/npm git subtree on 2026-07-30
# These samples are ACTIVELY MALICIOUS code published by real threat actors.
# The harness keeps the zips encrypted at rest under the gitignored
# eval/samples/, extracts into a TempDir only for the duration of one scan, and
# executes nothing on the host: Layers 2/3 run inside the existing container with
# --network=none, a DNS sinkhole, a read-only /pkg mount, and a wall-clock cap
# via --docker-timeout. Never `npm install` one of these outside the container.
# `vectors` is `-` except for incidents with a published, attributable vector.
# The dataset carries no per-sample vector taxonomy, and inventing one would
# fabricate ground truth. Entries with `-` contribute to the overall detection
# rate and to the "which vector fired" breakdown, not to per-vector recall.
# `layers` is aspirational for Layers 2/3: the sandbox cannot fetch dependencies
# (--network=none + --offline), so any sample declaring dependencies yields an
# empty behaviour profile. The runner reads declared_deps from the extracted
# package.json and marks such entries dyn_valid=false, excluding them from the
# dynamic denominators rather than counting a vacuous PASS as precision.
